headline_scope.description: Current crown representatives contribute one set of service estimates per crown. Lower vegetation and hidden earlier unmatched detections are excluded. Values remain sensitivity scenarios; overlapping crowns can still count shared canopy. V5.2: 457 crowns drawn from a source record (9,052 m²) are counted with a flag (v6.2: 240 confirmed or drawn by a reviewer, 2 retired by a correction, 215 await confirmation); 77 drawn crowns 2–3 m tall are low canopy and not counted.

assembly.note: v6.1 streams, records and summaries with the four v6.2 changes applied to the affected trees and layers.

v5_changes: All 3,149 survey tiles completed successfully, including 16 retries.
V5 crown dimensions use 2024 point-cloud structure and aerial NDVI.
Every previous ALTO tree ID remains available. Current representatives link to original source records.
Crown identity uses actual containment and polygon intersection; shared crowns can contain several trees.
Unverified notable-tree positions are excluded from automatic crown attachment. Council renumbering has a versioned crosswalk.
Existing service and trunk sensitivity equations use the new crown dimensions once per representative. Earlier estimates remain in the full records.
Lower vegetation is available as separate layers and excluded from tree service totals.
Earlier crown outlines are retained outside the new survey footprint.
KYTE nearby matching uses the same current representatives. Saved observations and original IDs remain valid.
limitations_v5: Segmentation changes are not tree removals or growth observations.
A crown can contain more than one tree, and a multi-stem tree can remain split.
Three polygon validity repairs and four area corrections are logged; original outputs are preserved.
Growth-form predictions and historical matching were not refitted on v5 crowns.
The earlier fitted forecast is applied to current crown height; its original benchmark does not validate this transfer. Nearby-history weighting awaits refreshed spatial matching.
The service, DBH and root coefficients remain sensitivity assumptions requiring field calibration.
Summed crown areas include overlaps and are not a measure of land-cover percentage.
v51_changes: Restored 4,661 crown associations across 4,362 existing crowns: 3,518 Auckland Transport, 470 Council Parks and 673 earlier LiDAR records.
Retained all 6,238,420 original source IDs, source positions and existing survey histories. Former generated representatives remain accessible as linked records.
Recomputed affected model scenarios once per representative crown using the existing V5 equations; no recalibration or new ground measurements.
Rebuilt map markers, property summaries, release totals and KYTE nearby suggestions from the same repaired snapshot.
Preserved the two KYTE visits already accepted since V5. Incoming submissions and researcher review decisions were not changed.
Crown unlinked replaces No crown: failure to link a source position does not establish tree absence.
v51_limits: The V5 polygon geometry, including known holes and clipped boundaries, is unchanged.
28,735 audited candidates still need review; proximity alone is not sufficient for automatic attachment.
A restored crown association does not certify that every linked source record describes the same organism.
The private researcher workbench retains its earlier dataset baseline and saved assessments until a separate, versioned migration.
v52_changes: Joined 3,088 records that V5.1 left unlinked to a crown: 1,043 linked and 1,456 probable matches to existing V5 crowns, and 589 on 534 crowns drawn from the 2024 returns at the record position.
1,456 crowns are now represented by a register or other source record instead of a LiDAR detection; 844 records joined a tree that already had a marker and are listed in its profile.

A protected or notable tree never loses its marker: 1 protected record now represents its crown in place of an ordinary record, and 14 protected records on a crown already represented by a protected tree keep their own marker; estimates are counted once per crown. Protected trees on the map: 3,570 (V5.1 3,570).
Record-seeded crowns are drawn faintly and await confirmation. 457 are counted in totals and services with a flag (crown_source record_seeded_v52); 77 are 2–3 m and follow the low-canopy rule.
A new default-off layer, Council recorded positions, shows each joined record's original source point and a line to its crown top. Source coordinates are unchanged in the full record.
Recomputed service scenarios once per representative crown with the existing V5 equations; superseded representative estimates are archived in the release database.
Retained all 6,238,420 original source IDs, positions and histories, the V5.1 continuity repair, the two accepted KYTE visits and all researcher review decisions.
v52_limits: Precision by class: linked 0.989 hold-out, 47/48 blind audit; probable 0.936, 33/37; drawn from the record 31/37 audit only. Audit intervals are wide.

20,704 records went to researcher review and are unchanged on the map, and the drawn-crown links await confirmation there; 13,613 records outside V5 and 2024 point-cloud coverage stay unlinked with that reason.
4 drawn-crown links were excluded because their crown enclosed an existing V5 crown; those records are unchanged.
V5 polygon geometry, including known holes and clipped boundaries, is unchanged. Record-seeded crowns are proposals until confirmed.
A link does not certify that every record on a shared crown describes the same organism.
v6_changes: Growth form for 3,352,099 crowns: 2,771,551 shown, 580,548 not yet determined. Every shown growth form is a model estimate; recorded species stay the species shown.
Crowns are drawn with smoothed outlines of the same V5 cells (area preserved); V5.2 record-seeded crowns smoothed the same way.

Service estimates changed for 2,918,424 representatives (PHASE2_DECISION 13.9): reweighted by the growth-form probabilities where a call is shown (2,749,679), the flagged evergreen default where it is not (168,745, previously the legacy image-model class). Recorded species keep their estimates.
Display rules: r15 with the V2 palm guard (1,028 crowns), palm-type medium calls outside the isthmus shown as "possibly" (0), deciduous worded by flight date (late June from day 166).
Retained every V5.2 record, link, marker, source position, history, review decision, accepted KYTE visit, V5 growth-form field and service row (in the database).
v6_limits: Growth form is a coarse class, not a species. Shown calls were about 94% right on the 600-crown blind test outside the isthmus (design-weighted); conifer and palm-type cells rest on small samples.
Tree fern uses the V5 palm leaf area and trunk curve until a tree-fern value is chosen.
Crowns drawn from a record in V5.2, crowns outside the V5 survey and records without a crown have no growth-form estimate.
Outlines smooth the V5 cells; V5 crown boundaries and sizes are otherwise unchanged (crowns over 60 m² remain about 20% smaller than human outlines).

corrections.note: Every accepted correction in config/corrections/corrections.jsonl carried by v6.3 (corrections_v63.py); corrections on tree pages read in tree numbers and plain names (public_summary).

v61_changes: Permanent tree numbers for all 4,200,336 map trees (T + 6 Crockford base-32 characters + a check character), in the map features (tn), the full records (tree_number) and an alias table of 19,376,165 keys (data/tree_ids) that resolves every record ID, v4 and v5 crown key ever published, and tombstones for the 7,405 LiDAR detections removed before the 9 Sep 2026 release. Links: https://alto.tfwelch.com/tree/<number>.

Corrections ledger applied in full: 14 applied (record moves, crown merges, reviewer outlines, a near-canopy crown linked to its record, a reviewer species, a KYTE visit moved to the tree it photographed), 17 recorded on the tree record, 318 already true, 5 awaiting review.
Retained every v6 record, link, marker, source position, history, estimate and growth-form field in the database.
v61_limits: Reviewer outlines change the crown area; the height stays the v5.2 measurement of the crown drawn from the record.
v62_changes: Crowns drawn from a record that a reviewer confirmed: 278 crowns (317 confirmations in the corrections ledger) now carry the confirmed evidence tier (very likely a tree), a solid outline and confirmed wording; so do the 5 crowns a reviewer outlined, and the 4 records a reviewer linked to another crown read as confirmed links. 248 crowns drawn from a record still await confirmation.

Palm detection shown from a C1 score of 0.2 (v6: 0.5) on crowns whose growth form v6 left undetermined, after a blind photo check passed its pre-set bar: 16,226 more crowns read "Likely palm or cabbage tree (palm-type crown seen in 2024 aerial imagery)"; their service estimates follow the v6 growth-form rules. Conservative post-hoc restriction (13 Oct 2026): the lower threshold is used only where v6 showed no growth form, so v6.2 shows fewer crowns than the pre-registered rule, which passed on the full set. In the check, the 49 newly shown crowns v6 had left undetermined were all palm-type, against 6 of 11 that v6 had shown as another class.
The change layer is described as the live v1 file (data/tree_change_v1.pmtiles, photo check 92% of shown changes real).
The near-canopy layer no longer draws the low-canopy polygon v6.1 made a tree crown (C00307); the polygon stays in the layer with canopy_class promoted_tree_crown.
Retained every v6.1 record, link, marker, tree number, source position, history, estimate and growth-form field in the database.
v62_limits: Three records on confirmed crowns were not themselves reviewed; their own links still read awaiting confirmation.
Palm detections at the lower threshold were checked on 60 crowns before the scope was restricted; v6.2 uses them only on crowns v6 left undetermined (49 of 49 palm-type in that check).

v63_changes: The benefit value is stormwater plus carbon: about NZ$76.7 million a year, down from about NZ$295 million a year in release 6.2, which also counted air quality and cooling. Air-quality and cooling dollars stay in each tree's full record, marked not release-eligible. Map ranks, comparisons among similar trees, Area, property totals and the release totals use the benefit value.

Release 6.2's benefit value added four services: air quality NZ$163.5 million a year (55.4%), cooling NZ$55.0 million (18.6%), stormwater NZ$74.2 million (25.1%) and carbon NZ$2.5 million (0.9%). Release 6.3 withholds the estimates of the 80 crowns whose height is not plausible (−NZ$9,352 a year) and values the 103 crowns drawn outside the v5 survey on their drawn outline (−NZ$671 a year).
PM2.5 removal and the cooling index are kept in the full record and not published: the PM2.5 method awaits confirmation of its sources.

Heights are checked: 80 map markers have a height that is not plausible (66 at 55 m or more; 14 below 55 m), and their estimates are withheld and left out of the totals; 2,692 have a height to check. Record-to-crown links are checked: of 42,491 linked records, 253 may be on a different tree from their crown and 5,556 are to check, on 4,188 map markers. Flagged crowns are left out of comparisons, Species maxima and the property tallest tree.

Height class replaces the life-stage label, and crown replacement time replaces the irreplaceability class. Crown replacement time: 80 years or more 284,679 map markers; 40–80 years 453,160; 15–40 years 1,040,238; 5–15 years 723,003; under 5 years 121,835. Not classed: 951,906 map markers (26.6% of the 3,574,821 map markers): 917,582 crowns under 5 m tall, 80 crowns whose height is not plausible and 34,244 map markers with no crown estimate. Tall tree, 25 m or taller, is a separate fact: 204,156 crowns.

3,824 map markers inside a Notable Group of Trees area carry the area's Schedule 10 item (3,266 crowns, 473 earlier detections and 85 records; 2,980 of those crowns had no link to Schedule 10, 334 on private land in 75 areas), and the 229 areas are a map layer. Whether a tree inside an area is one of the scheduled trees has not been established: 3,570 map markers are linked to Schedule 10, as in release 6.2.

Trees holding a Council point carry their Schedule 10 entry as the July 2026 schedule lists it: 2,480 entries, which together list about 4,787 scheduled trees; for 96 items every Council point lies on one crown.

A reviewer's note can travel through the corrections ledger: tree T162DYHP, where Council's point for item 1186 lies, carries one, and the field visit shown on it reads "A field visit found a tree at the Council point." Corrections on tree pages read in tree numbers and plain names.

Every source carries its licence; the 4,800 records derived from OpenStreetMap carry the Open Database Licence 1.0, and ALTO's noncommercial terms do not apply to them. Change since 2013 is release-eligible, with its limits.

The Species filter lists 1,028 species by Latin name under their common names, across the 56,258 map markers with a recorded species. 11 misspelled or outdated Latin names read their accepted names (3,546 records), checked against the iNaturalist taxonomy (accessed 17 Oct 2026); the name as supplied stays in each record. The 1,205 kauri survey records read Kauri.

i-Tree reference heights are stored in metres (kauri 165 ft is 50.3 m). Pūriri (952 records) reads evergreen broadleaf and cabbage tree (720 records) palm or palm-like; i-Tree's classes are kept beside them.
v63_unchanged: Tree numbers, positions and crown outlines: release 6.2's. The map shows 3,574,821 map markers and 4,200,336 tree numbers; 1,447 crown outlines, nearly all earlier crowns outside the v5 survey, are cleaned to their polygon parts, with the same area.
Growth form, Council positions, the near-canopy layer and the Change since 2013 file are release 6.2's.
Every value release 6.3 retires stays in each tree's full record: the life-stage label, the irreplaceability class, the air-quality and cooling dollars and the release 6 PM2.5 rate.
v63_limits: The height checks rest on the 2024 LiDAR survey and published maximum heights; a real tall tree can be flagged where its returns were misclassified.
The record check's third rule reads the growth-form model, which can itself be wrong (a kauri read as broadleaf), so one rule alone marks a record only to check.
The group-area flag places a marker inside Council's indicative overlay; it does not establish that the tree is one of the scheduled trees. The overlay may have changed since it was retrieved.
Height class and crown replacement time use ALTO planning defaults for four growth forms; species within a growth form vary. Trunk diameter and root zones keep the release 5.2 growth-form class.

Benefit estimates are not independently validated; they remain sensitivity scenarios. Stormwater is priced at NZ$3.50 per cubic metre of avoided runoff (1.5 times in flood-prone areas) and carbon at NZ$50 per tonne CO2e; neither price is an audited Auckland value. Each crown's band is set by its valuation confidence (±30% for modelled medium, ±60% for modelled low).
v63_deferred: PM2.5 removal and the cooling index: published once the method's sources are confirmed and its check passes.
Plantation forest: crowns in exotic forest are classed by regrowth time like every other crown; release 6.3 does not overlay a land-cover map (LCDB).
Trunk diameter calibration and ranges: they need reviewed girth measurements; KYTE's girth missions collect them.
Crowns at the 400 m² merge limit: not re-segmented; they keep the note "at or near the 400 m² segmentation limit".
The benefit class of a recorded species, and accepted names from national name lists: the benefit estimates keep the growth-form class.
For a multi-tree Schedule 10 entry, the other crowns of the parcel: no "may be one of the trees" line yet.
Lighter map tiles, a packed full-record archive and a place index.
